decisions.reason: “Seemed to freeze” preserves the image without making the battlefield heat literally freeze.
The shorter phrasing keeps the distance and viewpoint.
“So could” clearly carries the narrator’s perception over to the Pavilion members.
“Thick” keeps the sense of dense killing intent in natural English.
The danger and sudden halt are preserved in idiomatic phrasing.
The concise line preserves that the narrator stopped him.
“Practically growled” captures the snarling quality of his shout.
The recast preserves that this was Sama Pyo’s own choice, not fate or misfortune.
The ellipsis convention is natural and preserves the pause.
“Huge” preserves the sense of Taishan’s unusually large eyes.
“Cut in” naturally conveys Namho speaking before the others could.
The shoulder-riding detail and its effect on Namho’s authority remain.
The dialogue keeps Namho’s meaning in concise, natural speech.
The angry-bull image and teasing rebuke remain.
The slap and stern scolding are both preserved.
The rhetorical rebuke keeps the source’s meaning and tone.
The removed attribution is redundant; the surrounding exchange already identifies Namho’s point.
SOL drops the repeated self-reminder “Don’t go yet” and fails to italicize the direct thought.
The struggle, lowered staff, and comforting gesture remain without the awkward trailing clause.
The turn toward the figures is preserved; “Then” fits the sequence.
The old man’s position and gaze remain; “unreadable” naturally conveys his deeply sunken eyes.
The deleted sentence merely repeats the immediately preceding identification.
The two-sentence recast preserves his titles and standing.
“Bent on revenge” naturally preserves his status as another avenger.
SOL’s “no longer” adds a prior change; the source says that at this moment the eyes reflected someone other than Sama Pyo.
The source means the enemy’s bloodline, not the enemy’s literal blood.
The surrounding radius and suffocating effect remain clear.
The source specifically names the overwhelming force as qi; SOL replaces that established term with “force.”
The split sentence preserves when and where the first meeting happened.
The reordered sentence preserves the Daoist’s lifelong devotion and gentle character.
The contrast and his humility as Sect Leader remain intact.
“Yet” preserves the turn while keeping the vessel image.
The source describes a past regret; SOL shifts it to a recurring present regret.
The response to Hyeoncheon’s sigh remains clear in natural phrasing.
The pronouns have clear antecedents in context and preserve who withheld the truth.
The woman as the source of Hyeoncheon’s information remains clear.
SOL drops the stepping-stone image and changes the stated scheme into a more specific claim about the woman’s intent.
The attempt to forget the information and the deepening suspicions are preserved.
The gear image and the way the signs fit together remain.
The split sentence keeps both the wrong information and the fact that only they bled.
“Lay” is a natural equivalent for the mountain’s location.
The added name clarifies which surrounding Disciples the source refers to.
The source uses the image of a battle beginning like lightning; “a bolt from the blue” changes it to surprise.
The pause after “No” preserves the correction and the slaughter’s one-sidedness.
The unceasing arrows and wall construction remain, with the defenders made explicit from context.
The human tide’s destruction of lives and the relationships lost are preserved.
SOL drops the source’s explicit wish to die heroically, though both versions keep fighting to the last breath.
The other Disciples’ shared wish and tearful eyes remain.
The concise line preserves that they survived.
The fragment preserves the necessity of surviving.
The escape, unexpected help, and contrast with the others remain.
The unequal distribution of luck is preserved.
The deaths and continued vulnerability of those who fled remain.
The scattering and further deaths and injuries remain without adding “one by one.”
“Yet” preserves the contrast with their escape.
The inability to return and the varying injuries are preserved.
The planted suspicion and Hyeoncheon’s realization during his recovery remain.
The timing—while he hovered between life and death and vowed revenge—is preserved.
The denied identities and the named enemies remain in a more natural construction.
The allies’ trusted role in guarding the rear is preserved in idiomatic English.
The question’s intimacy and low-key tone remain.
The source says he had recovered after three days; “barely recovered” preserves that completed recovery better than “begun to recover.”
The bear-gall bitterness and the moment their faces came to mind remain.
“Little more than servants” preserves the leaders’ subservience.
The anger rising in his chest and the woman’s revelation remain.
The source’s answer remains; the indefinite article does not change the sense.
The surviving Disciples and his purpose of confirming the answer firsthand remain.
The young man’s voluntary arrival and the timing before revenge remain.
The source says his way of speaking changed; “manner of address” narrows this to how he addresses someone.
The source gives his voice a metallic sound; SOL reduces that to a generic harsh edge.
The bowed head and ripples in a pool of blood are preserved.
The ellipsis convention is natural and preserves the pause.
The Korean uses the established title Perfected Being Hyeoncheon; SOL drops the title.
The disciples’ widened eyes and the killing intent bearing down on Sama Pyo remain.
“At once” preserves their immediate understanding.
The source presents this realization as a direct thought; SOL drops the required italics.
The source presents the name as a direct thought; SOL drops the required italics.
The enemy’s deserved death and heaven-defying crimes remain in a natural recast.
The sentence preserves that Sima Gong was not the only traitor to die.
The grief in the cry is preserved in natural phrasing.
SOL omits the source’s explicit distance; BASE at least preserves that the disciple crossed a substantial distance.
The disciple’s broken, interrupted speech remains.
The timing of Hyeoncheon’s turn before the cry became sobs remains.
The flag’s distant, angled position remains.
The two pieces of white cloth and their weak flutter remain as a continuation of the preceding sentence.
The source explicitly says the surrounding qi surged; SOL replaces qi with generic force.
SOL turns the disciple’s unspecified reaction into the specific claim that he was overcome with grief.
The two Zhongnan Sect traitors and the planned order of punishment remain.
“Gone somewhere” naturally preserves the afterlife image and unreachable destination.
“Just like that?” preserves the disbelief without adding a question about what punishment they received.
The source contrasts the pain with agony in his chest; SOL weakens that agony to “pressure.”
The repeated, faltering question remains.
“Flew into a rage” preserves the source’s anger without changing the event.
The source says the disciples had to swallow their breath; “catch their breath” suggests recovery instead.
“Stood his ground” conveys that Sama Pyo alone was unaffected by the pressure.
The forced words, endurance of the master’s qi, and Hyeoncheon’s darkening gaze remain.
The shorter question preserves the meaning and immediate reaction.
The debt and punishment owed for his father’s wrongs remain clear in natural dialogue.
The silence, bow, and continuation are preserved.
“Grievances” preserves the bereaved people’s unresolved resentment.
The heart’s inability to be filled again is preserved.
The source repeats the image of filling a hole; “mend” changes that image to repair.
The repeated attempts to forget and the lasting hole are preserved in natural English.
The loss from a single mistake and the regret it leaves remain.
The deleted sentence is repeated in the following sentence, which names Sama Pyo and explains why he is there.
The reason for his presence and his wish to choose a different path remain.
The blood-debt rule remains, with the established term Murim.
The source identifies the sword as being at Perfected Being Hyeoncheon’s waist; SOL drops the established title.
